why: rule-links says anything mentioned that has a destination gets a link the first time it is named -- a PR, a session, a rule, a file -- and had no mechanical check at all until this predicate (tools/precedent_reply_check.py's require_no_bare_pattern). Added 2026-09-20 after a reply in a downstream consumer repository mentioned 'PR #21' with no link, and nothing caught it before the person had to notice and ask. Declared advisory rather than blocking: markdown links are stripped from the whole reply once, up front, so a thing correctly linked on its FIRST mention and named bare again later in the same reply still matches -- a known imprecision (rule-links only requires the first mention to carry the link), not a bug, and not yet worth refusing a turn over. 2026-10-19: blocking, with dated session branches and file paths in code font added (Morgan: "Don't we have practice rules so when you mention files you always give links?", after a Boildown named a branch, a section and a practice with no link). Advisory had meant unseen: main() drops an advisory finding without telling anyone, so this had never reached a session. The imprecision that justified it is fixed: a name linked anywhere in the reply now covers its later bare mentions.
